scenario: A 71-year-old man has a white count of 42,000 that is mostly lymphocytes. The smear shows ruptured cells. He feels well and has small nodes. A classmate starts chemotherapy the same day because any high white count is acute leukemia.
question: Which disease fits the ruptured cells, and why is same-day induction the wrong reflex?
options: CLL, and many patients are observed at first
Acute lymphoblastic leukemia, so blasts should fill the smear
CML, so a low enzyme score and a huge spleen are expected
A viral lymphocytosis that ruptures cells the same way
Iron deficiency, because fatigue is assumed
correctAnswer: CLL, and many patients are observed at first
citation: Kumar V, Abbas AK, Aster JC. Robbins and Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease. 10th ed. Elsevier; 2021.
examTakeaway: Smudge cells in an older adult with a high lymphocyte count are the fragile cells of CLL.
